object_description: low pavilion-like volume following the river
design_condition: The low volume follows the river over a long distance, opens a sequence of break areas toward the landscape, and remains compatible with the residential slope context through its reduced apparent height.

positive.statement: The lying volume convincingly accompanies the course of the river and opens attractive break areas between building and river.

position.target: river-aligned lying volume and break areas
position.rationale: Elongated footprint visibly follows the diagonal river direction, with openings distributed along the landscape-facing edge.

positive.statement: On the slope side, the building volumes are compatible with the small-scale residential buildings because they do not appear at full height.

position.rationale: Low massing is approximated along the upper, slope-facing side of the elongated footprint.

positive.statement: The shifted skylights reduce the massive volumetrics to a size comparable to the residential buildings.

position.rationale: Repeated roof interruptions are visible along the upper footprint and localized near roof level.

positive.statement: The footbridge over the river leads directly in front of the main entrance and provides a convincing connection to the existing school area.

position.rationale: Entrance-side connection is approximated at the slope-facing end of the sampled footprint.

positive.statement: The disciplined grid creates a lively central space and supports diverse learning cluster arrangements.

position.rationale: The top view shows a structured central zone between the elongated perimeter edges.

positive.statement: The skylights provide zenithal light to the learning landscape and additional light to adjacent school rooms.

position.rationale: Learning area is placed beneath the visible skylight sequence at upper-middle building height.

positive.statement: Structural discipline achieves flexibility and efficiency while creating manageable units that invite appropriation.

position.rationale: Regular repeated bay pattern is visible across the footprint and elevations.

positive.statement: The structural and material organization is very carefully developed, including a convincing system separation.

position.rationale: Building-wide organization is anchored to the clearly repeated envelope and level bands.

positive.statement: The prefabricated concrete construction allows very different usage scenarios over the lifespan of the building.

position.rationale: Construction judgment is anchored to the repeated structural bands visible on the elevations.

negative.statement: The steep road embankment begins directly at the building and provides no attractive space for the ground-floor rooms on the slope side.

position.target: steep road embankment and slope-side ground-floor rooms
position.rationale: Upper footprint edge is used as the slope-side ground interface.

negative.statement: Views from the street down into the classrooms are unwanted.

position.rationale: Privacy concern is anchored to the slope-facing side where street overlook is described.

negative.statement: The lack of emergency access, deliveries, and disabled access seems impractical.

position.target: emergency access, deliveries, and disabled access
position.rationale: Access deficiency is approximated at the constrained slope-side approach.

negative.statement: The connection to paths and roads on the slope side appears unmanageable, with the main footpath awkwardly routed around the building.

position.rationale: Circulation issue is located along the upper edge of the long building mass.

negative.statement: The distinction between green and paved areas remains schematic and leaves no further statements.

position.rationale: Landscape interface is approximated beside the lower, river-facing edge.

negative.statement: A learning cluster on the entrance level creates potential conflict with the break area in front of it.

position.target: entrance-level learning cluster and break area
position.rationale: Potential conflict is placed near the entrance-side lower zone.

negative.statement: Overall stability and seismic safety should be checked for a more economical structural solution.

position.target: overall structural stability and seismic safety
position.rationale: Structural concern is anchored to the repeated low-rise frame visible across elevations.

negative.statement: The foundation on strip footings running in only one direction could be simplified.

position.rationale: Foundation judgment is placed beneath the visible longitudinal structural organization.
